Issued at 257 AM MDT Sat Aug 29 2026

I have returned after a break and this pattern reminds me of one of 
my favorite types of candy from my youth and the movie it was from. 
The movie was "Willie Wonka and the Chocolate Factory", the original 
with Gene Wilder. And the candy was the "Everlasting Gobstopper." 
And this reminds me of the pattern we have been in since the middle 
of July, except I would title this "The Everlasting Monsoon."

And this is no exception this morning, as we continue to have a 
plume of monsoonal moisture streaming northward over the area, 
mainly the northwest half of the region. Dewpoints are also 
rather high, most locations in the 50s. I know people from the 
East Coast or Gulf Coast are laughing at this statement, but 
that is rather high in this part of the country. Precipitable 
water values also remain rather high, topping out at over an 
inch in some locations, which is close to 200 percent of normal.
Most guidance continues to put the main impact west of the 
Continental Divide. The HREF ensemble gives a greater than 1 in 
2 chance of a half an inch or rain or more across much of 
western Wyoming through 7 am Sunday. And, with the rain being 
enhanced by a shortwave and approaching cold front, the forcing 
gives me greater confidence in the solution. Exact positioning 
of the storms is still not certain and there are a couple of 
factors against excessive rainfall. One is cloud cover, it may 
be fairly substantial today. This would limit instability and 
possible thunderstorm development. The other is that we do have 
some decent flow at 500 millibars, as much as 40 knots on some 
models. This should keep the storms moving. There could still be
some training though. We continue to have a Marginal risk of 
excessive rainfall across the area as well. So, we will 
continue the Flood Watch as is for now. Like tonight, showers 
and possible thunderstorms will continue through the nighttime 
hours as well.

We also have to talk about the possibility of severe thunderstorms. 
The entire state is under a marginal risk with western Sweetwater 
and southern Lincoln Counties under a Slight risk of severe 
thunderstorms. Hodographs are generally of the unidirectional 
variety which would lead to wind and hail being the main threat.
We did have some wet microbursts on Friday and this looks to 
once again be the main threat today. The Storm Prediction Center
has roughly the southern half of Wyoming in a Conditional 1 
area for convective wind (wind gusts to 75 mph), and this looks 
reasonable given the largely straight hodographs and decent mid 
level forcing and wind. Again, the main concern against the 
severe weather may be cloud cover which could limit instability.
So, severe storms are not definite but the possibility is 
definitely there. 

The cold front will move across the area on Sunday. Much drier air 
will move in behind it through the area, bringing below normal 
precipitable waters from west to east across much of the area by 
sunset on Sunday evening. This should also help shut off or limit 
the amount of convection. The main area of concern on this day 
would be southern and eastern portions of the area. We still 
have a Marginal risk of excessive rainfall on this day, roughly
south of an Evanston to Casper line. As for stronger 
thunderstorms, it would be more limited and largely across the 
usual suspects of Johnson and Natrona Counties where more 
instability would build before the cold front arrives. And then,
to quote Monty Python, "Now for Something Completely 
Different".

Much cooler air will move in behind the front, and with a clearing 
sky, light wind and the longer nights of late August, it will get 
quite cool. And this brings the possibility of potential below 
freezing temperatures and possible frost. The best chance would be 
across the western valleys. The NBM ensemble gives around a 1 in 2 
chance of portions of the Jackson Valley falling to 32 degrees 
Monday morning. Most other locations are less than 1 out of 3 
though. The chance of temperatures below 28 remains very low though, 
less than 1 out of 10. At this point, if there is any frost it would 
be patchy. There is still time to evaluate, so we will let the 
day shift take another look.

On Monday, monsoonal moisture will make another push northward 
although it looks to be a later arrival at this point except in 
far southern Wyoming. The night time arrival could limit 
excessive rainfall though with little instability and most 
precipitation just being showers despite precipitable waters 
again rising to over 150 percent of climatological normals. 
Tuesday looks like more widespread activity. Wednesday may be 
rather active as well, although another approaching shortwave 
and weak cold front and drier air behind it may dry things out 
somewhat. Timing is still uncertain this far out though.
